basis: The registered northern extension and its palette edit in village-approach-v1
userDirection: Some leaves are fine, but not everywhere. Broad areas may be plain dirt or grass.
finalEdit:
Use case: precise-object-edit, simplify terrain ground cover.
EDIT INPUT 1, the existing northward game-ground master. Input 2 is the fixed camp-edge reference. Keep the EXACT overhead viewpoint, framing, image scale and the shape and location of every DIRT PATH. Keep the chestnut/umber/muted olive colour progression already established, with the warmer orange camp contact at left and bottom.

The user explicitly dislikes the repetitive red/orange leaves everywhere. REMOVE ALMOST ALL of the red/orange leaf and flower-like shapes from the editable new ground. This is a substantial simplification, not a slight thinning. The leftmost 10% and bottommost 12% are locked contact strips and must remain unchanged. Elsewhere, smoothly transition out of those contact strips into much quieter terrain:
- About half the new ground is uninterrupted BARE BROWN DIRT: softly painted granular earth, a little tiny grit, no leaves or leaf-shaped markings.
- About a third is irregular areas of low, flat muted olive/green grassy ground. It should read as grass surface, not a carpet of leaf shapes or flowers. Broad natural patch shapes; no individual raised tufts, tall plants or bushes.
- Some darker earth and softly worn pale brown ground between these areas for natural local variety.
- Only a few sparse leaf clusters near edges: at most about 8 small scattered clusters in the editable new area, each containing a few small subdued brown/rust fallen leaves. No bright red/orange flower-like shapes. Most land should contain NO leaves.
Also reduce the dense repeated brick-shaped pattern in the new open ground. Keep the few existing paving remnants at the top of the dirt trail, but allow the rest of the terrain to be mostly plain soil or grassy surface.

Preserve the wide northbound DIRT trail and the narrower eastern dirt fork in precisely the same positions, with naturally worn edges. The paths must remain continuous into the existing lower border and out of the top/right edges. Do not turn them into stone roads. Do not alter the locked bottom and left contact strips.

Keep a crisp hand-painted game-ground appearance, soft even daylight, flat terrain plane. No new objects, trees, bushes, tall plants, rocks, buildings, fences, water, people, borders, labels, vignettes, grid or shadows from absent objects. No image blur. Output one opaque wide master at the same 3072:1660 aspect ratio, highest resolution available. This should look visibly much calmer: plenty of bare dirt and plain grassy ground, occasional leaves only.
